steps.what: Read device age and last cost band
Mark which devices must stay in service
Draft replacement lines from the asset rows

loop.output: one line per device id with year, reason and cost band
loop.check: Every line cites a device id on the asset list and copies the cost band or leaves it blank
loop.stop: One draft; drop a line with no device id
loop.why_not_simpler: The reason to replace this year is not a fixed age rule

steps.what: Add the year totals on the sheet
Sign this year's replacement budget
File the signed replacement budget

tasks.design: Device id, age, site and the last cost band come from the {OPS_SYSTEM} onto a {SPREADSHEET}. A bounded draft in {DOCS} writes one replacement line per device and leaves the cost blank when no band exists. The sheet's own total adds only numeric bands. The architect signs one budget version for the year. Nothing is ordered in this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Age, failures and cost notes lived in different sheets, so a line could not show which device it replaced.
tasks.enabler_now: Device id, in-service year and last cost band can be columns, and a total can ignore a blank band.
tasks.still_hard: Which devices the firm will pay to replace this year is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The architect decides the year a device is replaced and signs that budget version.

ambition.what: Refresh the replacement year when a device fails, not only in the annual budget

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to rebuilding the asset list. The funding choice stays. The architect can refuse a line that has no device id.

reach.task: Say which sites must stay in service
reach.learn: Which device ids are funded this year and which cost bands were blank

evidence.claim: A replacement budget in a mid-size firm is an asset list, a year and a sign-off. The hard part is which devices wait, not the total.
A blank cost band must stay blank. Filling a price the record does not hold would invent a number the sign-off cannot trust.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends at a signed replacement budget. Raising a purchase order is later work.

Input contract: device id, site, in-service year, last cost band, failure note, keep-or-replace. Producer of the asset row is the inventory. Producer of keep-or-replace is the service owner. A missing cost band stays blank and is excluded from the total.
The meeting prior is about a fifth of the time and is kept as the sign-off. Use the spreadsheet's own total and the inventory export before custom code.
unknowns: Where the last cost band is stored.
Who may sign the budget when the architect is absent.
Which devices have no in-service year.
research_questions: What share of devices have no cost band?
How often does the signed year differ from the drafted year?

already_counted.description: Architect edits reasons the draft overstates
Funding judgement stays with the architect

incremental.description: Add a column when a new device class needs its own replacement rule
Service owners correct a keep-or-replace mark sent for the wrong site

approvals.approved_version: replacement budget version signed for this year
the same signed replacement budget version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many devices have no id or no cost band, so the architect still builds the list by hand. The high case assumes clean rows and a native total, but every funding choice stays in the sign-off. Purchase orders are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hear the customer need and file the note

steps.what: State the network need and the site
Pass the internal deadline and priority
Read the constraints already on the design
Draft questions for the blank fields

loop.input: need mail, deadline and the blank-field list
loop.output: questions that name only a blank field
loop.check: Each question names a field that is empty on the form or the mail
loop.stop: One list; if nothing is blank, return no questions and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: What the customer will refuse is not a field that can be known in advance

steps.what: Meet to hear the customer need
Sign the needs note from the meeting
File the signed needs note

tasks.design: The customer contact states site and need in {EMAIL}. The service owner adds deadline and priority on a {WORKFLOW} form. A bounded list in {DOCS} drafts questions only for fields that are still blank. The architect meets the customer and signs one needs note. No design is drawn in this task, and no automated speaker joins the meeting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Needs were remembered from calls, so the next design could not show which sentence the customer had actually said.
tasks.enabler_now: Site, need, deadline and priority can be fields, and a question list can point at the blanks only.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing what the customer will not accept still happens in the meeting.
tasks.human_edge: The architect decides what the need really is and which constraint is firm.
tasks.altitude: The question list is shorter to prepare. The meeting does not shrink. The architect can refuse a needs note that has no site.

reach.task: Confirm the filed need matches what was said
reach.learn: Which needs note version is signed and which fields were left open

evidence.claim: Finding a customer need in a mid-size firm is a meeting. A question list can be prepared. The meeting cannot be replaced by a form.
Digest [S26] says chatbots disclose that they are automated from 2 August 2026. This design keeps the meeting with a person, so that duty is not triggered.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends at a signed needs note. Drawing the design is a later task.

Input contract: site, need text, deadline, priority. Producer of the need is the customer contact. Producer of deadline and priority is the service owner, including what sales or marketing staff have already passed on. If the site is blank, the question list says so and the meeting starts from the mail.
The conversation prior is right and is kept. Use the form's required fields before custom code. No chatbot speaks to the customer.
unknowns: Whether the customer will use the form or only the meeting.
Who may sign the needs note when the architect is absent.
Which sites have no existing design to read constraints from.
research_questions: What share of needs notes are contradicted by the next design review?
How often is the site still blank at the start of the meeting?

already_counted.description: Architect drops questions the mail already answered
Meeting time stays with the architect

incremental.description: Adjust the blank-field list when the need form gains a field

approvals.approved_version: needs note version signed from this meeting
the same signed needs note version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the need arrives only in the meeting, so the question list is unused and almost all time stays in the call. The high case assumes a short form, but the meeting and the sign-off are not treated as saved. Design drawing is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set platform, interface and bandwidth rows

steps.what: Read the needs note and capacity rows
Draft platform, interface, bandwidth and schema

loop.input: needs fields, capacity rows and the column template
loop.output: rows for platform, interface, bandwidth and routing schema
loop.check: Each row cites a requirement id present on the needs note
loop.stop: One draft; drop a row with no requirement id
loop.why_not_simpler: Whether a row is mandatory is not a column the template can know

steps.what: Decide which requirement rows are mandatory
Check which interfaces are exposed
File the signed requirement set
Accept the requirement constraints

tasks.design: The signed needs note and the capacity rows supply site, volume and constraint. A bounded table in {SPREADSHEET} drafts platform, interface, bandwidth and routing schema, each row tied to a requirement id. The architect decides which rows are mandatory. The security analyst checks exposed interfaces. The set is filed in {DOCS}. Nothing is ordered or applied in this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Platform and bandwidth choices were sentences in a design, so a later spec could not tell which number was mandatory.
tasks.enabler_now: Requirement id, platform, interface, bandwidth and routing schema can be columns checked against the needs note.
tasks.still_hard: Which row is mandatory, and which exposed interface is acceptable, are still judgements.
tasks.human_edge: The architect decides the mandatory rows and the bandwidth the site can actually use.

ambition.what: Reopen requirement rows when the volume forecast changes, not only at design start

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to retyping known platforms. The mandatory call stays. The architect can reject a row with no requirement id.

reach.learn: Which requirement rows are mandatory and which interfaces are still open

evidence.claim: Hardware and software requirements in a mid-size firm are a table plus a decision. The table can be drafted. The mandatory flag cannot.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so these rows are not turned into a live change or an order in this task.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends at a signed requirement set. The detailed specification and any purchase are later tasks.

Input contract: requirement id, site, platform, interface, bandwidth, routing schema id, mandatory flag. Producer of the need is the signed needs note. Producer of volume is the capacity rows. A row with no requirement id is not marked mandatory.
Use the spreadsheet's own columns and the document approval flow before custom code. Routing schema here means the routing pattern, not a staff routine.
unknowns: Who sets the mandatory flag when the architect is away.
Whether bandwidth is a number or a range in the source note.
research_questions: What share of requirement rows are later changed in the specification?
How often is an interface marked exposed and then dropped?

already_counted.description: Architect corrects a bandwidth the draft copied from the wrong row
The mandatory decision stays with the architect

incremental.description: Add a column when a new interface family has to be named
Analysts recheck an interface the set still marks exposed

approvals.approved_version: requirement set version signed for these ids
the same signed requirement set version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the needs note is prose, so the table is filled by hand and the draft rarely helps. The high case assumes clean ids, but the mandatory decision and the exposure check stay manual. Orders and live changes are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Take the signed requirement rows
Draft the network specification from those rows

loop.input: requirement rows and the pack template
loop.output: node list, chart, configuration and recommended technology
loop.check: Every line cites a requirement id on the source
loop.stop: One draft; drop a line with no requirement id
loop.why_not_simpler: The recommended technology is a judgement, not a lookup on the row

steps.what: Mark lines whose device id is unknown
Sign the specification version
File the signed specification
Take the config table for the build

tasks.design: The signed requirement rows are the only source. A bounded pack in {DOCS} drafts the node-and-link list, the {SPREADSHEET} chart, the equipment configuration and the recommended technology, and every line must cite a requirement id. A fixed check marks lines whose device id is not on the {OPS_SYSTEM} inventory. The architect signs one specification version. The pack is not applied to live gear here.
tasks.previous_blocker: Diagrams, charts and configs were separate files, so a device id could differ across them with nobody noticing until build.
tasks.enabler_now: Requirement id and device id can be checked across the pack, and unknown ids can be marked before sign-off.
tasks.still_hard: The recommended technology, and whether the pack is buildable, still need the architect.
tasks.human_edge: The architect signs the specification version the operator will build from.

ambition.what: Issue a specification version with every accepted requirement change, not as one final pack

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to retyping tables. The recommendation and the sign-off stay. The architect can refuse a line with an unknown device id.

reach.task: Build from the signed configuration table
reach.learn: Which specification version is signed and which device ids were unknown

evidence.claim: A network specification in a mid-size firm is a pack of lists, tables and configs. The hard part is whether the lines agree, not the headings.
Digest [S3] says a document product can fill metadata from a prompt, and the vendor warns the fill can be wrong. That is title, owner and version, not the configuration body.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so this task files a specification and does not apply it.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends at a signed specification. Building the network is later work.

Input contract: requirement id, device id, node, link, configuration line, recommended technology, chart measure. Producer is the signed requirement set. A line with no requirement id is dropped. A device id missing from the inventory is marked, not invented.

Diagrams are a node-and-link list in the document store, not a separate drawing product. Use that store's template and the inventory export before custom code. The meeting prior is low and this task keeps the sign-off on the document.
unknowns: Which requirement rows have no device id yet.
Who may sign a specification when the architect is absent.
Whether recommended technology must name a single option or a short list.
research_questions: What share of specification lines cite a device id missing from the inventory?
How often does sign-off change the recommended technology?

already_counted.description: Architect rewrites the recommended technology in the draft
Sign-off time stays with the architect

incremental.description: Update the pack template when a new configuration family appears
Operators send back a config line they cannot build

approvals.approved_version: specification version signed with these device marks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes requirement rows are prose, so the pack is written by hand and the id check finds little. The high case assumes clean rows, but the architect still rewrites the recommendation and signs every version. The build is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Budgets, needs notes and specifications start from fields. The architect still decides what to fund, what the customer needs, and which requirement is mandatory.
reach: Service owners see the replacement year on each device instead of a slide.
Network operators build from the signed specification, not from a meeting recollection.
skills_to_grow: Tie a replacement line to a device id, a year and a cost band from the last purchase.
Write a requirement as platform, interface, bandwidth and routing schema.
Check a specification line against an inventory id before signing.
role.ambitious_version: The replacement year, the customer need and the specification all cite the same device ids.
